Consult Summary:
- 27-year-old patient with 3 days of profuse watery diarrhea, intermittent lower abdominal cramping, nausea/vomiting (worse with milk), and subjective fever; clinician impression: acute gastroenteritis; advised oral rehydration, clear fluids/soft diet, acetaminophen (paracetamol), avoid alcohol, and follow-up if not improved in 48 hours.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Profuse watery diarrhea with intermittent lower abdominal cramping.
- Onset/duration: Began ~3 days ago.
- Course: Ongoing; not improving yet.
- Character/frequency: Watery stools occurring almost every hour while awake.
- Pain: Crampy lower abdominal pain, midline, intermittent; patient-estimated severity ~6/10.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Nausea; vomiting present (not as prominent as diarrhea).
  - Vomiting triggered after milk ingestion; patient is trying to avoid milk.
  - Subjective fever/feeling hot; no measured temperature.
  - Passing urine less frequently but still urinating.
- Pertinent negatives: Denies blood in stool.
- Intake: Trying to drink water; feels like fluids “go straight through.” Ate lunch today; stool remained loose.
- Sick contacts/exposures: Brother with similar illness for ~5 days and possibly improving. No clear trigger identified; no specific food/takeaway exposure identified.
- Timeline summary: Symptoms started ~3 days prior to visit; persistent frequent watery diarrhea with intermittent cramps; nausea/vomiting with milk exposure; subjective fevers; decreased urinary frequency.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported; “otherwise fit and well.”
- Medications: Paracetamol recently for symptoms (dose/route/frequency not documented); no regular medications.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with mother and sister; brother does not live with patient.
- Occupation: Office-based government job in Central London; attempting to continue working despite symptoms.
- Tobacco: Social smoker (occasional cigarette, e.g., on Fridays).
- Alcohol: Occasional beer on weekdays; increased intake on some Fridays; binge drinking once or twice a month (exact units not specified).
- Diet: Usually buys food; does not typically eat with family.

Family History:
- Father with colon cancer (“third stage” per patient report); further details unknown.

Physical Examination:

Investigations:
- None performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis (presumed infectious)
  - Assessment: 3-day history of profuse watery diarrhea, midline crampy abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting (milk-triggered), subjective fevers; brother with similar illness supports infectious etiology. No blood in stool.
  - Plan:
    - Oral rehydration: Use oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte) over the counter.
    - Hydration/diet: Clear fluids; soft diet (e.g., soup, mashed foods); gradually advance as tolerated.
    - Symptom control: Paracetamol for fever/pain (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Avoid alcohol during recovery.
    - Follow-up: If not improving within 48 hours (1–2 days), call back for reassessment; further investigations may be needed if signs of dehydration or persistent symptoms.

- Issue 2: Risk of dehydration
  - Assessment: Very frequent watery stools (~hourly while awake) with decreased urinary frequency.
  - Plan:
    - Emphasize oral rehydration solutions and adequate fluid intake.
    - Monitor urine output and overall hydration; seek care if worsening or unable to maintain hydration.

- Issue 3: Family history of colon cancer
  - Assessment: Father with colon cancer; no acute red-flag lower GI bleeding reported by patient.
  - Plan:
    - Not specifically addressed in this visit; noted for history.

General plan items:
- Safety-netting provided: Return/call back in 48 hours if not improving; earlier if worsening or dehydrated.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure) not recorded.
  - No physical examination documented.
  - No objective hydration status assessment (mucous membranes, orthostatics).
  - No stool characterization beyond “watery” (e.g., mucus, volume) or travel/food exposure details.
  - No documentation of recent antibiotic use, sick leave/work note needs, or immunization status.
  - Medication dose/route/frequency for paracetamol not documented.
- Internal conflicts: None clearly identified.
- Transcript quality: Minor audio gaps/interruptions and occasional incomplete phrases; overall content interpretable.
